_doc: Architecture counts the pre-push ratchet holds (scripts/cmux-next/guardrails.py runs scripts/cmux-next/arch-ratchet.py; the method is scripts/cmux-next/arch_counts.py, whose docstring defines every row). A push may not raise a ratcheted row's total, in the code or in this file's totals, nor swap a counted global, broadcast or layer edge for another; when one drops, rerun `scripts/cmux-next/arch-ratchet.py --update` (the only writer). The one escape is a dated exception: add {"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "row": "<row>", "allow": <n>, "why": "...", "author": "<who wrote it>", "owner": "<who removes it>", "receipt": "Review (<reviewer, not the author>): SHIP at <40-hex sha>", "expiry": "YYYY-MM-DD"} as a new file plans/cmux-next/arch-exceptions/<id>.json (one entry per file, <id> a short unique slug such as the PR number, so two pushes that add one never conflict; never append to the exceptions list below, whose old entries are read with the files as one list; an entry with no independent receipt, owner or expiry allows nothing); the push that adds it may raise that row by n, and the next --update folds it into the totals and marks it with applied_sha (an applied entry is never edited or removed). --update refuses a rise that no pending exception covers, except a rise that commits already on origin/feat-cmux-next made past the hook (a GitHub merge, --no-verify): it records that one with a generated applied entry whose raised_by names those commits. A generated entry allows no rise in any push's code, and the push that brings it is re-checked: its commits must be on origin/feat-cmux-next, after the old measured_sha and in the new one, named by no other entry, and its allow at most their rise. Every blocking_allow_escapes site also needs an escape_reviews entry (path, text, owner, author, receipt, expiry, state): a push that adds a site with no reviewed entry is refused, and --audit lists unreviewed and expired ones. Never CI.

It runs once from CmuxNextApp.main (CmuxNextApp.swift:40) before NSApp exists, before LaunchWarmup and CEF start, so no frame exists that could wait.
